_note: Every parameter that changes a computed figure. Infrastructure (database, API keys, rate limits, log level) is not here - it belongs in the environment, because it cannot change an answer. A change to this file changes the digest, and the digest is stamped into every result's calculation_basis, so a stored verdict records the parameterisation that produced it. Environment variables still override any value here; GET /framework reports which ones did.

swot._note: A metric becomes a factor only once it clears a relative band around its benchmark, then lands in a 1-5 impact bucket by how far past the band it sits. Inside the band it produces nothing, which is why four empty quadrants is a valid output.

market_structure._note: HHI bands are the US DOJ/FTC 2023 Merger Guidelines, not invented. An unnamed residual share is treated as an atomistic fringe, which biases HHI down - documented, and the reason every sector on a filer population comes back UNCONCENTRATED.

matrix._note: Attractiveness is a weighted sum of four 1-5 axes; weights must sum to 1.0. Thresholds at 2.5 and 3.5 are the documented GE-McKinsey cut points. Borderline flags a point within margin of a boundary, because a verdict that close is not a verdict.

pricing._note: A cost-plus anchor blended with the competitor benchmark, then adjusted for the shared-feature quality gap and floored at cost. Blend weights must sum to 1.0. The adjustment is capped so a feature-score gap cannot run the price away from the market.

porters._note: Buyer power and substitutes have no proxy in this data, so the composite reports how many of the five forces were actually scored and refuses below min_input_coverage rather than averaging over absent ones.

sensitivity._note: The exact minimum change in any single input that flips the quadrant, solved analytically because attractiveness is linear in its axes. FRAGILE below fragile_threshold; knife_edge is the distance at which the verdict should not be relied on at all.

uncertainty._note: Analyst-supplied {low, mode, high} estimates, not distributions estimated from data. Seeded, so a rerun reproduces exactly. Entropy of the quadrant distribution is the stability measure; its maximum is log2(3) because there are three quadrants.

portfolio._note: PROJECT-DEFINED ALLOCATION RULE, not part of the GE-McKinsey framework. Harvest units contribute this share of revenue to the pot; floors are satisfied first or the request fails outright.

validation._note: Permutation null for the backtest. The seed is the one the published results in docs/validation_results.md were generated with - changing it invalidates the comparison to those numbers.

benchmarks._note: A sector median is published only at this sample size; below it the sector is withheld rather than published thin. This is a methodology choice, which is why it lives here and not with the EDGAR transport settings.

trend._note: Movement smaller than this on a 1-5 axis is reported as stable rather than as a trend, because two to five filing periods cannot support a slope.
